newsitem.title: USA: Dealers, analysts survey members on muni disclosure.
newsitem.headline: Dealers, analysts survey members on muni disclosure.

text.p: Groups representing municipal bond dealers and analysts nationwide are surveying members to see how effectively the market is implementing the SEC's 1994 continuing disclosure rule, Reuters has learned.

PSA The Bond Market Trade Association (PSA) and the National Federation of Municipal Analysts (NFMA) want responses to the four-page study by close of business April 8, according to a copy of the study.

The two groups have scheduled a two-hour national symposium at PSA headquarters in New York City on April 17 where a live panel will discuss and field questions on industry progress with the Securities and Exchange Commission's two-and-a-half-year-old rule.
The amendments to SEC's Rule 15c2-12 bar dealers from underwriting bonds unless issuers pledge to provide ongoing disclosure of financial information and material events.
Dealers must have systems in place to monitor material events that could impact the bonds they recommend to buyers.

Jeff Baker, chairman of the NFMA and vice president of Chase Manhattan Bank, warned recently that some bond issuers are not complying with the rule. SEC officials have agreed to meet with analysts shortly to hear their concerns.
Baker said the group is prepared to release names of at least 25 issuers, mostly health care authorities, that analysts say are not complying with the rule.

The PSA/NFMA survey includes 12 sets of questions. Dealers and analysts are asked, for instance, to rate the quality and quantity of disclosure for eight market sectors: health care, housing, general obligation, transportation, power, student loans, water and sewer and leases.

The survey asks whether it is easier or harder now to get official statements, annual financial statements and material events notices from issuers since enactment of SEC's disclosure rule. It also asks whether there has been no change.

Touching on a key concern of analysts, the survey asks, "Have you found that some issuers will only make their annual financial statements and updated operating data available through the national repositories, rather than directly."
